newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castor futures gain on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian castor futures gain on speculative buying.

text.p: Castorseed September delivery rose 6.0 rupees per quintal to 1,150/1,151 rupees on speculative buying on Thursday after touching a high of 1,154/1,155 rupees per quintal, traders said.
They said the buying was prompted by import enquiries for castor oil from China.
Reports of higher arrivals in India's western state of Gujarat had a dampening impact on prices, traders said.
Last week Indian exporters had sold 6,400 tonnes of castor oil to China at $695 per tinne, said Dilip Thakkar, a leading trader.
"We are getting more enquiries from Chinese buyers," Thakkar said.
On Thursday, arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region rose to 19,000/20,000 bags (75 kg each) against 15,000 on Wednesday.
In edible oils, groundnut oil was steady at 357/358 per 10 kg on a limited arrival of 40/50 tonnes while demand was at a low ebb. In Rajkot, spot groundnut oil was steady at 565/570 rupees per 15 kg.
In Bombay, imported palmolein two rupees to 271/272 per 10 kg on fresh demand. Marketmen predicted prices to slide following the arrival of about 6,000 tonnes of palmolein at Bombay port.
